categories.main_business_segments: Verisk operates primarily in a single business segment: Insurance. This segment provides data analytics, technology, and decision support solutions to property and casualty (P&C) insurance providers, as well as to life insurance, annuities, specialty insurance, and marketing clients. The company previously operated Energy, Specialized Markets, and Financial Services segments, but these were divested by early 2023.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Verisk leverages proprietary and contributory data assets, advanced analytics, machine learning, artificial intelligence, and cloud-based software platforms. The company collects, processes, and analyzes billions of insurance records, maintains one of the world's largest private insurance databases, and develops predictive models, actuarial tools, and workflow automation solutions. It also utilizes geospatial data, remote sensing, and field data collection for property and risk assessment.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Verisk's primary customers are P&C insurance providers, including all of the top 100 U.S. P&C insurers, as well as global reinsurers, InsurTech companies, specialty insurers, brokers, managing general agents, and government agencies. The company also serves life and annuity insurers, self-insured employers, third-party administrators, and insurance repair contractors, with a growing presence in international insurance markets.
categories.geographic_coverage: Verisk's operations are global, with a primary focus on the United States, which accounts for the majority of revenue. The company also has significant operations and customer bases in the United Kingdom, Canada, Ireland, Continental Europe, Australia, New Zealand, and Asia-Pacific regions. Its solutions are used in over 120 countries, and it maintains offices in more than 20 countries worldwide.
categories.supply_chain_position: Verisk operates as a data, analytics, and technology provider, positioning itself as an upstream and midstream supplier within the insurance value chain. It provides foundational data, analytics, and workflow solutions that are embedded in the underwriting, pricing, claims, compliance, and risk management processes of insurers and related stakeholders.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Verisk's strategic priorities include driving consistent and predictable growth within insurance, modernizing core solutions through cloud technology and advanced analytics (including AI and machine learning), expanding into adjacent markets (such as life insurance and specialty lines), and enhancing operating efficiency. The company invests heavily in R&D for new data assets, digital workflow tools, and innovative analytics, and pursues selective acquisitions to augment capabilities.
categories.revenue_model: The company primarily generates revenue through annual or long-term hosted subscription agreements, which accounted for approximately 81% of 2024 revenues. Additional revenue streams include transactional and advisory/consulting services, as well as licensing of proprietary data, software, and analytics. Most contracts are prepaid, providing strong cash flow visibility.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Verisk faces competition from internal insurer analytics teams, other statistical agents and advisory organizations, regional property inspection firms, InsurTech startups, consulting and IT services firms, and specialized software vendors. Key industry peers include S&P Global, Moody’s, Equifax, TransUnion, Fair Isaac, Gartner, MSCI, and CoStar. Verisk is a market leader in U.S. P&C insurance analytics, with deep industry integration and broad solution coverage.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2024, Verisk reported revenues of $2.88 billion, up 7.5% from 2023, with an EBITDA margin of 57.6% and net income of $958 million. The company has demonstrated consistent revenue and EBITDA growth, strong cash flow generation, and high operating leverage. Recent years saw portfolio simplification through divestitures, with a focus on core insurance analytics and continued organic and acquisitive growth.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Verisk differentiates itself through its proprietary and contributory data assets, deep insurance industry expertise, long-standing client relationships, and the scale to drive innovation across the insurance ecosystem. Its solutions are highly embedded in client workflows, offering predictive analytics, regulatory compliance, fraud detection, and operational efficiency, which help clients improve risk selection, pricing accuracy, and claims outcomes.
